title: What does PaymentChannelClaim do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of PaymentChannelClaim and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, PaymentChannelClaim redeems an authorized cumulative XRP claim or changes a payment channel's closing state. [1]

A signed claim authorizes a total amount for that channel, not an additional payment of that amount on every retry. The channel balance and authorized ceiling constrain redemption. Closing and renewal flags have specific permissions and timing rules. Confirm the resulting channel balance and any remaining funds rather than counting signatures as separate settlements. [1]

The PaymentChannelClaim reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using PaymentChannelClaim, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
